propositions: A single pending queue entry disables the O(1) fast path marker store-wide, causing every subsequent write to perform a full O(store-size) directory walk until the pending set empties

The marker's all-or-nothing write logic (clearing on any pending, writing only when scan finds nothing) does not track which tickets were checked, making it unable to scope subsequent probes to just those live entries
On a 4,938-ticket live store with one pending entry, each write incurs ~1,200-1,330 ms (full scan cost) instead of the O(1) quiet-path 0.110 ms

The proposed live-set marker extends the marker to record ticket ids with enqueued not-DONE entries, allowing scoped probes to reduce only those tickets (O(backlog)) when marker is fresh but not quiet

Scoped probes do not rewrite the marker to preserve the TTL measurement from the last full walk, maintaining the existing append-during-scan race bound while avoiding full walks during sustained backlogs
